scope: One synthetic conversation; diagnostic across five dimensions, not a statistically reliable benchmark.
source: Thomasgudan/kapibala-sales-dialogues; CC BY 4.0; synthetic, not an authentic recorded sale.

understanding_customer_needs.reason: Recognizes workflows and integrations; workload, business impact and measurable success are not established.

discovery_questions.reason: Systems question is relevant; customer volunteers most needs and security concerns, while other salesperson questions concern logistics.

value_explanation.reason: Explains relevant workflows but the claimed automation percentage is not substantiated and customer-specific value is not measured.

objection_handling.reason: Honest verification promise followed by customer-reported acceptance supports resolution; does not independently verify certification.

next_step_clarity.reason: Onboarding contact has an owner/deadline; contact timing must not be conflated with a confirmed kickoff date.

transcript_facts.fact: Customer reports receipt/security review and completed signup. This is not independent certification verification.
Onboarding team promises contact within three business days to arrange kickoff; meeting date is not confirmed.
Customer raises handoff and security concerns; the salesperson asks about systems and offers signup/document logistics.

findings: Next steps correctly contain only onboarding contact/scheduling.
Discovery reason incorrectly credits salesperson with uncovering customer-volunteered security criteria.
Value reason treats claimed automation percentage as substantiated without independent source evidence.
Next-step reason overstates contact within three days as kickoff scheduling within three days.
Improvement 2 proposes checking document receipt despite the customer already reporting receipt and acceptance.
Security-document follow-up is superseded by later customer-reported receipt/signup and the onboarding scheduling commitment.
